slides.heading: Community Organizing Participatory Action Research
slides.subtitle: Empowering communities to study and solve their own health problems — the people are the researchers.

slides.heading: What COPAR Is
bullets: Community Organization — plan the solution; Participatory Action Research — active participation.
Action research promotes development; the people are the researchers themselves.
Role of the nurse: facilitator, assist, teach.
Role of the people: leader — assess, plan, implement, evaluate.

slides.heading: Emphases of Community Organizing in PHC
bullets: People working together to solve their own problems.
Internal organizational consolidation before external expansion.
Social movement first, before technical change.
Health reforms within broader social transformation.
It is value-based, people-centered, participative, democratic, developmental and process-oriented.

slides.heading: Phases of COPAR
rows: Simplest phase — preliminary social investigation, site selection (GIDA criteria, ≥100 families), courtesy call, networking.
Deepen social investigation, immersion/integration, identify potential leaders, form core group (5–8).
Plan solutions, build the Community Health Organization (CHO), elect & train officers, team building.
Mobilization (people's power), program implementation, monitoring & evaluation, train BHWs.
Continue training, develop medium/long-term goals, turnover, self-reliance.

slides.heading: Criteria for Potential Leaders
bullets: Active listener; a resident in good standing with moral ascendancy.
Influential and respected (charismatic); willing to work for the community; desires change.
Currently NOT holding a leadership post in other organizations (e.g., barangay).

slides.heading: Population Pyramids
rows: Increased birth rate, increased death rate.
Low birth rate, aging population (long life expectancy).

terms.definition: Science & art of preventing disease, prolonging life and promoting health through organized community effort.
Assessment (collect/analyze data), Policy development (advocacy), Assurance (services effective, available, accessible).

slides.heading: Roles of the PHN
bullets: Clinician/health care provider, Educator, Advocate, Manager, Case manager.
Collaborator, Leader, and Researcher/Epidemiologist (uses findings to drive policy).

slides.heading: Key Takeaways
bullets: COPAR phases: Pre-Entry → Entry → Organizational → Action → Sustenance.
The people lead and research; the nurse facilitates.
PHN core functions: Assessment, Policy development, Assurance.
